articles.title: Back to the Middle: Engineering Customer Experience in the Age of AI Agents
articles.excerpt: The recent surge in conversation around AI agents has done more than introduce a new technology trend. It has unsettled long-held assumptions about how digital value is created and delivered. Analysts are now openly debating whether the multi-billion-dollar Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) industry could be facing an existential reckoning as AI systems and autonomous agents advance rapidly

articles.title: The Hidden Architecture of CX: Body, Mind, and Soul
articles.excerpt: Customer experience is ultimately delivered through thousands of small human decisions. A frontline employee deciding how far to go for a customer. A manager interpreting signals from frustrated clients. A team navigating pressure while trying to resolve a difficult situation. When those human systems are healthy, organisations consistently deliver remarkable experiences. When they are not, even the most sophisticated technology struggles to compensate.

articles.title: The three pillars of unbeatable CX: ease, authenticity, and trust
articles.excerpt: What does it take to survive — and thrive — through the internet boom, the booking.com wave, and now the rise of agentic AI? I recently sat down with Kate Couling, co-founder of World Journeys, a bespoke travel agency operating out of New Zealand for over two decades. The answer she gave me wasn't about technology, pricing, or marketing. It came down to three words: ease, authenticity, and trust.

articles.title: Channels Are Delivery Mechanisms. Journeys Are the Product.
articles.excerpt:
There is a phrase I hear in boardrooms constantly. Every time I hear it, I tell myself I should reward myself with a treat.

That phrase is "channel strategy."

Not because channels don't matter. They do. Your app has to work. Your website has to be good. Your contact centre has to function. But the moment an organisation starts using channels as the primary unit of design, investment, and accountability — something quietly breaks. And the customer feels it long before leadership does.

items.bio:
Kate Couling is a co-founding director of World Journeys and has worked in the travel industry since her early twenties. Her career began the way the best ones often do — travelling the world on a budget, arriving into cities late at night with nothing pre-arranged, navigating bureaucracy and language barriers, and proving she could figure it out on her own.

That formative experience is the foundation of everything World Journeys does today. Kate and her fellow directors built the agency on a simple but powerful mission: to design journeys they would undertake themselves. Every itinerary is crafted from personal knowledge and direct experience — not brochures, not third-party reviews. The team has worked in the industry for over 30 years and continues to travel regularly, because at World Journeys, staying current is not optional — it is the job
items.name: Kate Couling

Previously, David held senior leadership roles at Vodafone, where he led the Digital Business unit spanning eCommerce, Customer Care, and Omnichannel strategy. His career is marked by large-scale digital transformation and continuous improvement initiatives centered on customer value.

With over 20 years of experience across global organizations, David specializes in digital business models, customer experience, and technologies that drive efficiency and growth. He is also a recognized voice in artificial intelligence applied to marketing and customer experience, and a founding member of the AI Forum in Spain (https://www.foroia.es/).

He regularly speaks and teaches on AI, digital transformation, and the future of customer experience.

items.bio:
Oleksandr (Sasha) Zablotskyi is a digital experience and transformation leader with deep expertise across e-commerce, telecommunications, and financial services. Currently serving as Head of Digital Channels at Openbank — Santander's digital-first banking platform and now the largest European digital bank by deposit volume, with operations across Spain, Germany, Portugal, the Netherlands, the US, and Mexico — Sasha leads the evolution of customer journeys at one of the most ambitious digital banking platforms in the world.

Over the course of his career, Sasha has worked at the intersection of product, customer experience, technology, and digital strategy — helping organisations rethink how customers interact with digital services in an increasingly connected world. From pioneering Ukraine's first eSIM solution at lifecell (including a cross-company one-minute activation flow built in partnership with Monobank) to building omnichannel commerce at Eldorado, his experience spans the full arc of digital transformation — from legacy retail to modern banking infrastructure.
items.name: Oleksandr (Sasha) Zablotskyi

items.bio:
Mohamed Soliman is the Regional Vice President at Energy Exemplar, one of the world's leading platforms for energy market modelling and optimisation. Over the past two decades, Mohamed has operated at the intersection of strategic vision and commercial reality — scaling Energy Exemplar's MENAT and CIS operations, contributing to its A$1.6B acquisition, and driving a 12x revenue transformation in Siemens' steel sector. His foundation is rigorous: a B.Sc. in Electrical and Digital Control Engineering from Cairo University, an MBA, a DBA, and a Private Equity & VC certification from Wharton.

What makes Mohamed the right voice for this episode is his ability to take some of the most mathematically complex problems in industry — multi-objective optimisation across thousand-node energy networks — and explain them in language any leader can act on. He has led the GCCIA Interconnection Program underpinning regional grid stability across the Gulf, advised sovereign funds, regulators, and policymakers across 28+ countries, and built a reputation as "the quiet force" who unlocks deals where strategic insight has to meet commercial realism.
items.name: Mohamed Soliman

Through her work at GameChangers People & Talent, she helps leaders accelerate their impact while building and sustaining high-performing teams in an increasingly dynamic business environment.

With a career spanning more than two decades across the US, Europe and Asia Pacific, Alexei brings a rare global perspective to one of the most complex, fast-moving and trust-critical spaces in customer experience: how you design for something people are never meant to think about.

episodes.role: Department Chair, Information Systems and Technology, IE University
episodes.about:
AI is everywhere — but real value remains elusive.

In this episode of The CX Algorithm Podcast, Dr Eslam Afifi is joined by Kiron Ravindran, Professor and Department Chair of Information Systems and Technology at IE Business School, to cut through the noise and examine what’s actually working — and what isn’t — in today’s AI-driven organisations.

Together, they explore why so many AI initiatives struggle to deliver ROI, despite unprecedented investment and capability. The conversation unpacks the growing gap between AI output and human understanding, the rise of “attention-span AI,” and how polished machine-generated answers can create an illusion of expertise rather than better decision-making.

A key focus of the episode is the shift from automation to AI augmentation — why the most successful organisations are using AI to enhance human judgment rather than replace it. Kiron shares insights on where AI creates genuine productivity gains, where it consistently fails, and why IT productivity hasn’t improved at the pace many leaders expected.

The discussion also looks ahead to the next wave of AI — from intelligent agents to context-aware systems — and what leaders must rethink to design work that is more focused, human-centred, and outcome-driven.

This episode is for leaders and practitioners looking to move beyond AI hype — and design technology that truly creates value.

Together, Eslam and David unpack what this re-intermediation means for customer experience, emotional connection, advertising, trust, and leadership.

His career spans more than 20 years across global organisations and is marked by large-scale digital transformation and continuous improvement initiatives centred on customer value.

David is also a recognised voice in artificial intelligence applied to marketing and customer experience, and a founding member of the AI Forum Spain. He regularly speaks and teaches on AI, digital transformation, and the future of customer experience.

episodes.about:
AI is moving faster than most decision cycles — and leadership has never been more complex. In this episode of The CX Algorithm Podcast, Dr. Eslam Afifi is joined by Ana Herranz, executive & HR coach and co-founder of Game Changers for People and Talent, to unpack what leadership needs to become in the AI era: not more technical… but more human.

Ana introduces a practical “inner algorithm” for modern leadership built on three elements:

1) The Mind (clarity & innovation) Under pressure, leaders default to convergent thinking (safe answers, repeat what worked before). Ana explains why innovation requires shifting to divergent thinking — creating cognitive space, asking “what are all the possible answers?”, and modelling learning over perfection.

2) The Body (presence & regulation) Leadership is a physical act. Stress shows up in tone, posture, breath, speed, and patience — often before words do. Ana shares why healthy habits matter, how simple rituals (like breathing and grounding) help shift from survival mode to leadership mode, and why asking for feedback is critical because body language can reveal what you don’t notice.

3) The Soul (purpose & authenticity) Purpose isn’t a single discovery moment — it’s built through action and attention. Ana shares a simple journal exercise: track daily activities and rate each by energy and engagement to identify patterns, find “flow” moments, and adjust your role (sometimes by delegating the energy-drainers rather than changing companies).

They also discuss a key practical challenge: your first three months in a new executive role. Ana explains why leaders must read the organization’s business cycle (growth vs mature vs restructuring), adapt their approach, and secure quick wins/pilots to earn buy-in.

Finally, they connect it all back to AI: how AI can create space for better thinking, why leaders must rethink team skills and structure (including working alongside AI agents), and why the real differentiator going forward is the human behind the leader.👤 About the Guest

Ana Herranz is an executive and HR coach with over 15 years of experience working across academia and industry. She has delivered more than 3,000 one-on-one coaching sessions with executives worldwide and facilitated over 400 workshops for large organisations. Ana is the co-founder of Game Changers for People and Talent, where she supports leaders and organisations in building human-centred, future-ready leadership.

episodes.about:
What does it actually take to build customer relationships that last — not just satisfy, but genuinely endure? In this episode, Dr Eslam Afifi sits down with Kate Couling, founder of World Journeys, a bespoke luxury travel agency that has thrived for over 20 years through the internet boom, the rise of online booking platforms, and now the emergence of agentic AI.

Kate unpacks the three principles that have been the backbone of World Journeys since day one: ease of doing business, authenticity, and trust. But as the conversation unfolds, it becomes clear these are not three separate ideas — they are a chain reaction. Get the first one right, and the others follow naturally. Skip one, and the whole thing collapses.

The episode covers how World Journeys manages complex multi-destination itineraries for high-end clients, how they handle crises when things go wrong on the other side of the world, what luxury actually means when you strip away the brand names, and why the most powerful signal of customer trust is a client who sends you a single sentence — and nothing more.

Whether you work in travel, financial services, government, or any service-driven industry, this conversation will change how you think about customer engagement, human connection, and the role of AI in the future of CX.

What if the same algorithm running thousand-node energy grids is the one quietly running every customer experience strategy too — whether we name it that way or not?

In this conversation, he translates that experience into language CX leaders can act on Monday morning.

Whether you lead CX, design customer journeys, build AI-enabled experiences, or sit at the strategy table watching the same trade-offs come up week after week, this episode gives you a sharper lens for thinking about the problem and a cleaner framework for solving it.

episodes.about:
Most organisations have a channel strategy. Very few have a journey strategy. And that gap — invisible from the inside, painfully obvious from the outside — is quietly undermining customer experience in banking, telecoms, retail, and beyond.

In this episode of The CX Algorithm, Dr Eslam Afifi sits down with Oleksandr (Sasha) Zablotskyi, Head of Digital Channels at Openbank (Santander), to challenge one of the most deeply embedded assumptions in CX design: that channels are the right unit of measurement, investment, and organisational structure.

Sasha's argument is direct. Customers have never thought in channels. They think in tasks, in needs, in moments. The channel is a delivery mechanism — invisible when it works, painful when it doesn't. The journey is the product. And until organisations restructure around that idea — not just in strategy decks, but in their org charts, their metrics, and their AI roadmaps — the gap between intent and experience will persist.

Whether you lead CX, product, digital, or customer strategy — this episode will challenge how you think about the systems your organisation has built, and who they were actually built for.

Think about your last payment. The screen, the colours, how it felt. Chances are you remember almost nothing — and that's exactly the point. In this episode of The CX Algorithm, we unpack the art of invisible customer experience design: how the best payment experiences succeed by disappearing, and why trust — not speed — is the real product.

Host Dr Eslam Afifi sits down with Alexei Krasnov, a customer experience and product design leader in payments across Asia Pacific, for a practitioner's look at designing what people never consciously notice — engineering trust, calibrating friction, and building experiences for a customer who is increasingly not even in the room, because an AI agent is transacting on their behalf.

Whether you work in customer experience, product design, UX, fintech, payments, or financial services — or you're just curious how the invisible systems around you are built — this episode will change how you see every tap, swipe, and checkout.

Think about your last payment. The screen, the colours, how it felt. Chances are you remember almost nothing — and that's exactly the point. In this episode of The CX Algorithm, we unpack the art of invisible customer experience design: how the best payment experiences succeed by disappearing, and why trust — not speed — is the real product.

episodes.role: Head of Research at COX Architecture
episodes.about:
EPISODE DESCRIPTION

What if the most overlooked part of customer experience isn't digital at all — but the physical room your service happens in? In this episode of The CX Algorithm, Dr Eslam Afifi and design researcher Dr Jacqueline Baker (Head of Research, COX Architecture) unpack the servicescape: the idea that space, light, sound and layout are part of the service itself, shaping how customers and staff behave before anyone forms a conscious thought.

Servicescape is a decades-old concept from service research, yet most CX, service design and customer journey work still treats the environment as a backdrop. This conversation puts it back at the centre — bridging architecture, environmental psychology and neuroscience to show how the built environment drives behaviour, emotion and commercial outcomes.

You'll hear how our nervous system appraises a space in seconds, how designers tune the "dials" of ambient and spatial conditions on purpose, and why the room shapes employee experience as much as the customer's. Jacqueline shares the airport study linking natural light, greenery and quiet zones to longer dwell time and higher spend — achieved by improving wellbeing, not exploiting it — and draws a sharp ethical line between enhancing an experience and manipulating it.

If you work in customer experience, service design, CX strategy, retail, healthcare, hospitality or the built environment, this episode gives you a new, measurable variable to design with: the room.

episodes.role: Senior Global Marketing & Strategy Manager, Cabot Corporation
episodes.about:
EPISODE DESCRIPTION

What if your best growth year was never really yours, just the market doing the work? In this episode of The CX Algorithm, Dr Eslam Afifi sits down with Jonathan Rabiei (Senior Global Marketing & Strategy Manager, Cabot Corporation) to pull apart one of the most comfortable illusions in business: that a rising market is proof you are good at growth.

When demand outstrips supply, growth hides everything: weak pricing, a clogged innovation pipeline, thinning customer intimacy, and a business that looks like it is winning while it quietly stops earning. Drawing on more than 18 years across specialty and battery materials, Jonathan reframes growth not as a sales target but as a whole-company system: the way R&D, operations, supply chain, commercial and finance together create, deliver and capture value.

You'll hear the five blind spots a booming market hides, the four questions that separate real growth from a tailwind, how Jonathan turned a "flat", written-off polymer segment into a core business in three years, and why retention is engineered far upstream rather than defended with discounts at the exit.
